topics.topic: OwnerSession representation of a pending confirmation with no revision or access version
questions: How does OwnerSession represent the new no-revision-and-no-access-version confirmation binding?
How is a pending confirmation represented when the confirmed action showed no revision or access version?

quotes: at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to, and the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced by the next one shown and cleared when used;

An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, or that it showed none when the action has
   neither (a record without a revision, A04 rule 3, among them), and its
   inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.
judgement.divergence: M11 requires every pending confirmation to carry a revision or access version, while A13 permits a pending confirmation explicitly bound to no such version; the owner notices whether a confirmation step for an unversioned action can be used.
judgement.why: The amended rule introduces an explicit no-version binding that the exhaustive OwnerSession facts do not represent.

bases.passage: at most one pending confirmation — its one-time value, the action, its target, the revision or access version and the inputs it is bound to, and the instant it was shown — made when a confirmation step is shown, replaced by the next one shown and cleared when used;

questions: Is A21 now reopened, and which affected category outcomes and tests must be reviewed again before it may remain PERFORMED?
Has the security review been repeated against the changed A04 and A13, or is A21 now reopened and no longer complete?

judgement.why: This is the same question already judged in P1 on the same changed A04, A13 and A21 passages.

precedent.topic: Whether A21 was reopened or the security review was repeated and reaffirmed after A04 and A13 changed
quotes: A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.
precedent.why: Because A04 changed and the concurrency category names A04, A21 is reopened; the unchanged PERFORMED label records the earlier performance but does not override the reopening rule.

topics.topic: Whether an identical file re-upload invalidates a pending confirmation and how file identity is determined
questions: If another upload replaces the session's file with byte-for-byte identical content and therefore the same digest, does the old confirmation remain valid?

If the next upload has the same digest as the file for which confirmation was shown—most simply, the owner uploads identical bytes again—does it invalidate the pending confirmation? What digest algorithm and file-identity rule make this decision?

quotes:
at most one uploaded import
file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

The uploaded file is kept in the owner session that uploaded it, in the
   process's memory only — never in the store, never on a disk — until the import is accepted, another file is uploaded in that
   session, or the session ends (M11); then it is dropped.

The mapping names
   the file by its digest. The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.

Confirming a mapping after another file was uploaded in the session is
   refused: the file it named is no longer kept.
judgement.divergence: One implementation accepts the old confirmation when the replacement upload has the same digest; another treats every accepted upload as a new file instance and refuses the old confirmation. The owner sees a committed import versus a demand for a new confirmation step.
judgement.why: The text binds confirmation to a digest but also says any later upload replaces the named file, without deciding whether byte-identical replacement preserves its identity.

witness.initial: Owner session S holds uploaded file F and a pending import confirmation bound to F's digest D and mapping choices P.
events: The owner uploads the same bytes again in S, replacing F with another upload whose digest is also D.
The owner submits the original confirmation with the same mapping choices.
outcomes: Registry accepts because the currently kept file has digest D and all bound inputs still match.
Registry refuses because the later upload replaced the particular uploaded file for which the confirmation was shown.
witness.observer: The owner sees either a completed import or a requirement to show and confirm the mapping again.
basis: The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface.

The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.

provenance.quote: at most one uploaded import file, replaced by the next upload and dropped when the import is accepted.

topics.topic: Whether stale-revision failure overrides the repeated same-state transition invariant
questions: Must A05’s invariant exclude same-state transitions that fail A04’s revision check?
Does the stale-revision rule override A05's formal invariant for a repeated transition, or must every transition to the already-held state be accepted?

judgement.why: P2 already decided that A05 applies only after every A04 check passes, including revision validation.

precedent.topic: Whether A05's repeated-transition invariant is conditional on passing A04 revision checks
quotes:
A transition to the state a record is already in, that passes every check
   of A04 rule 6, is accepted and changes nothing: archiving an archived project (R0-12), anonymising an anonymised
   one (R0-71), erasing an erased Customer (Primary actions), restricting a
   restricted Customer, lifting an unrestricted one, ending an ended
   relationship, resuming one that is not ended (R0-84), granting a project
   already in a session's set, making the active project active again,
   clearing an active project that is already clear, registering a registered
   session (R0-53).
precedent.why: A05 expressly conditions its repeated-transition rule on passing every A04 check, so a supplied former revision fails the revision check first.

topics.topic: Failure classification when a revision-bearing record receives no revision
questions: When the target currently has a revision but the action supplies none, is it refused as a missing required input at stage (4), or as stale at stage (5)?

quotes:
Every action that moves a Project's or a Customer's revision ("Revisions and
   times") states the revision it was made against: correcting, archiving and
   erasing a project; correcting a customer, erasing its contact data,
   restricting and lifting, ending and resuming the relationship.

A stated revision that is not the record's current one is refused as stale,
   and nothing changes (R0-35).

(3) that every record the action names exists —
   its target and any it newly names, such as a customer; (4) the
   values given (A02, A08, A22); (5) the stated revision or access version
   (A12); (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the
   set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict.
judgement.divergence: One implementation treats an omitted revision as a missing required value at stage 4; another treats it as a stated nonmatching value at stage 5 and returns stale. The owner and later error-contract authors observe different refusal reasons and precedence.
judgement.why: The rules require the action to state a revision but define only mismatching stated revisions, not how omission is classified.

topics.topic: Failure precedence between confirmation binding and stale-revision checking
questions: When a confirmed action on a revisionless record submits a revision despite a confirmation bound to none, is the first failure a confirmation-binding failure at stage (1), or stale revision at stage (5)?

quotes:
An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, or that it showed none when the action has
   neither (a record without a revision, A04 rule 3, among them), and its
   inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.

Every operation — read or change, of a service, Kernel or the owner —
   checks in one order, and the first failure is its answer; a stage that
   does not apply to it is skipped, and each check an operation states belongs
   to the stage of its kind: (1) the caller's authentication and its right to
   the operation (A09) — for the owner, a valid owner session (sign-in
   excepted, A13 rule 4), then for a change its CSRF value (R0-29), then a confirmation value where one is
   asked (A13);

(5) the stated revision or access version
   (A12); (6) the record's lifecycle — archived, erased, anonymised, not in the
   set, a customer's eligibility, a conflict.
judgement.why: The confirmation is bound to the step's explicit no-version fact and is checked at stage 1, before stale-revision validation at stage 5.

topics.topic: Failure precedence when deleting an anonymised project using its former revision
questions: When deletion of an anonymised project states the revision from before anonymisation, is the answer stale or the refusal that an anonymised project cannot be deleted?

judgement.why: P5 already judged this exact precedence question on the amended A04 and unchanged A05 passages.

precedent.topic: Which refusal takes precedence when deleting an anonymised project with a stale revision
quotes:
A revision stated for one is not its current one, and the action is
   refused as stale (rule 2): stage (5) of rule 6 applies to it, and comes
   before stage (6) and the refusals of A05 rule 4 — a resubmitted erasure that
   states the revision the record was erased from included; read again, the
   record shows no revision, and the action stating none is answered as
   State 0 and A05 say.
precedent.why: The amended A04 expressly places the stale-revision check before the lifecycle refusal in A05 rule 4, so the result is a stale refusal.
